1.why: The interface uses a clean sans-serif typeface with clear letter spacing and comfortable line height across all screenshots.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case with no italics, all-caps, or dense paragraphs; text is short and broken into brief lines.

3.why: Layout is a single centered card with large tap targets and simple stacking that appears designed for mobile widths, though only desktop-framed views are shown.

4.why: All instructional sentences are brief and use plain wording such as “Enter the six-digit code sent to your phone.”

5.why: A phone-number placeholder example (+447700900000) is provided, but no example format is shown for the six-digit verification code.

6.why: No screen requires reading more than two short sentences before the primary action is available.

7.why: The only code field is a manual text input for a six-digit value; no copy button or paste-friendly control for long secrets appears in any screenshot.

8.why: No QR code or alternative to typing the verification code is offered on the identity screens.

9.why: Standard email and tel inputs are present that browsers can autofill, but no explicit password-manager or autocomplete attributes are visible and the OTP field is a plain text box.

10.why: “Step X of 3” is shown at the top and the primary button (“Continue” / “Verify and continue”) is a large high-contrast block.

11.why: Each screen asks for only one main task—enter credentials or enter the code—with a single primary button.

12.why: The error banner only says “We could not complete that request. Please try again,” without stating what happened or what the user should do next beyond retrying.

13.why: The user can retry the code entry and use “Use different details,” but no control to re-request or reveal/hide a code is present.

14.why: The error message is generic, does not explain the actual problem, and gives only “Please try again” as guidance, though it avoids blaming the user.

15.why: No reading time limit is imposed, yet the code explicitly “expires in 10 minutes,” which is only moderately generous for entry.
